promotion_decision.verdict: negative: not cleared for a weekly submission slot
basis: No organizer-verified live score exists for this file and none is projected: the off-catalogue proxy criterion is calibrated within-family only.

Across artifact families the same proxy does not rank live scores: Spearman -0.057 (p 0.661) on 62 owner-reported anchors (the only significant term is credit-per-dot on the far collar, rho 0.252, p 0.048, and it is family-internal); the two direct off-catalogue emissions in the ladder scored 0.0512 and 0.0360 live against a 0.2778 incumbent.

The shipped raster measures criterion 0.3759 on the proxy truth (T 6350.0, S 33668.5, credit/dot 0.2117; evidence/h59j_emission_measurement.json), above the incumbent's 0.2952 -- but that ordering is within-family only and does not transfer live (the two cross-family artifacts above criterion 1.5 scored 0.036-0.051).

Emission design preferred spacing 3.0 px at 44090 dots (criterion 0.4606); the build used 30,000 dots because the owner live ladder is monotone down in budget, which makes the as-built arm the conservative choice, not the proxy-preferred one.

Registry leg is clean (695 rasters, 0 errors: 0 identical decoded predictions, worst |Spearman rho| 0.0636, worst exact dot-set Jaccard 0.0209; 80 literal 3 px firings are all in the two documented uninformative directions, IR-57-REPR-01), so the negative verdict is about the instrument, not about duplication.

Catalogue hide-and-recover holdout (HOLDOUT-DTI 0.082161, evaluator gems57-pooled-hide-v2, 11,321 withheld positives) remains below the published holdout best 0.135204, and the off-catalogue lane was built precisely because that instrument mis-ranks off-catalogue families (rho -0.544 with catalogue adjacency on live anchors).
promotion_decision.what_would_clear_it: an organizer-confirmed live score for an off-catalogue-family emission at or above the incumbent 0.2778, or a lane whose cross-family proxy ranks live scores (|rho| with p < 0.05 in the right direction) and whose top arm beats the incumbent's proxy criterion
